excerpt: Salt Security is a Palo Alto API security company, now also securing AI agents and MCP servers. Valued at $1.4 billion in 2022. What it does, who it suits and alternatives.
content:
Salt Security protects APIs, the interfaces that apps and services use to talk to each other. Its platform discovers the APIs a company actually has, including undocumented ones, checks their security posture against policy, and uses behavioural analysis to spot and block attackers probing or abusing them. Its website now leads with agentic AI security and MCP discovery, applying the same approach to AI agents and the Model Context Protocol servers that connect them to company systems.

According to its about page, Roey Eliyahu and Michael Nicosia founded Salt in 2018 when they saw that breaking applications into APIs was creating a new security risk. Eliyahu is CEO; the company's headquarters address is in Palo Alto, California. In February 2022 Salt announced a $140 million Series D led by CapitalG, Alphabet's growth fund, at a $1.4 billion valuation, with existing investors including Sequoia Capital, Y Combinator, Tenaya Capital, Advent International, Alkeon Capital and DFJ Growth taking part. The company said that brought its total funding to $271 million and came less than eight months after a $70 million Series C; Calcalist and SC Media covered the round.

Salt does not publish prices; its site offers a free trial and asks larger buyers to contact sales. It is aimed at security teams at companies with many APIs, such as banks, retailers and SaaS providers, and competes with API security tools from Akamai (which bought Noname Security), Traceable and Wallarm, as well as with features inside web application firewalls.

We have not used Salt Security for this page. It brings together Salt Security's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
